append.text: **Ps 28:2 *adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus* → *adorai o Senhor no seu átrio santo*** (= 95:8 word for word, grep — formula row). The Ps 28 blind reader listed *átrio* as unknown too (the second reader to do so); kept, the Latin's word; the Latinist passed it twice.

**Ps 28:4 *Vox Dómini in magnificéntia* → *a voz do Senhor com magnificência*:** the row's word, kept apart from 28:3 *Deus majestátis* → *o Deus da majestade* one verse before (MS1932's *majestosa* would merge them). **Listed as unknown by the Ps 28 blind reader too** — the second time; passed the Latinist twice.

Ps 28:5 *Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani* → *A voz do Senhor que quebra os cedros: * e o Senhor quebrará os cedros do Líbano* — participle and future of one verb, one Portuguese verb; *despedaçar* would crowd 28:6 *commínuet* (→ *esmigalhar*). No reader remarked.

Ps 28:6 *Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani* → *E, como a um bezerro do Líbano, os esmigalhará* (the cedars; the stylist's order, so that the mediant falls on the verb). The row's second place (grep: 17:43, 28:6); passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 28:6 *tamquam vítulum Líbani* → *como a um bezerro do Líbano* (the accusative marked by *a*: compared as a thing crushed); the blind reader heard it so. No remark.

Ps 28:6 *et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium* → *e o amado será como um filho de unicórnios* (the copula supplied, because the blind reader heard a bare *e o amado* as crushed too — the Latin's nominative forbids it). No reader remarked on *unicórnios*.

**Ps 28:9 *Vox Dómini præparántis cervos* → *que prepara as corças*, HELD against the Latinist:** minor on draft 1, MAJOR on draft 2 with the word unchanged (gender: *corças* are females, *cervos* is not). Held because *a voz do Senhor que prepara os servos* is a sentence a praying ear accepts and nothing in the colon names an animal; *veados* is a slur. The blind reader listed *corças* as unknown (the cost). **Proposal for a ruling:** *corças* wherever the colon itself does not name the animal (17:34, 28:9); *cervo* where it does (41:2 *quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum* — the verse's water and thirst; 103:17 *montes excélsi cervis*) — or *corça* everywhere for one word. *os cervos* is option 2 in Ps 28.

**Ps 28:9 *et revelábit condénsa* → *e que desnudará as matas densas*.** Not *ramos densos*: the Greek differs (here δρυμούς, 'woods'; 117:27b πυκάζουσιν), so by D15's test the two places need not share a word, and *ramos* would add a noun the Greek lacks here. Draft 1 *as matas cerradas* (the Brazilian collocation) was **heard by the blind reader as *serradas* (sawn)** — homophones; draft 2 *densas*, con-densa's own root. The Latinist passed both. *reveláre* of woods → *desnudar* ('lay bare', ἀποκαλύψει; *descobrir* is heard as 'find', *revelar* as disclosing); the blind reader listed *desnudará* as unknown.

**The active, Ps 28:7:** *vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades* → *a voz do Senhor que abala o deserto: e o Senhor abalará o deserto de Cades* — concútere and commovére are one Greek verb (συσσείοντος … συσσείσει), so one Portuguese verb, the active of this row's *ser abalado*. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 28:4 *Vox Dómini in virtúte* → *A voz do Senhor com poder*; 28:11 *Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit* → *O Senhor dará poder ao seu povo*** (God's virtus given; one word for the psalm's two places). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked; the stylist named 28:11 the best line. *força* (DRB) the option.

**Ps 28:11 *Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace* → *o Senhor bendirá o seu povo em paz*** — the row's verb, a people as object (the Latin's dative made direct, as current Portuguese construes *bendizer*); the stylist's best line; the blind reader heard a blessing. *abençoará* is the option.
Ps 28:11 *benedícet pópulo suo in pace* → *em paz*: the blind reader heard 'giving peace' first, 'while they are at peace' and 'peacefully' second — the Latin's range.

terms: | afférre (to God) | trazer (*Trazei ao Senhor glória e honra*) | open | Ps 28:1–2 (four times; the thing brought is first the young rams, then glory and honour — one verb carries both) and 95:7 (the same formula, three times), 75:12 *affértis múnera* (grep). ἐνέγκατε. *oferecer* is offérre's (65:15 *ófferam*); *render* fits glory, not rams; *tributar* is the Hebrew-family idiom. Safe at the *vós* imperative (past *trouxe*). DRB *Bring*; MS1932 *Oferecei / Rendei*. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. |

| vocative plural of persons, when the colon's build lets it be heard as an object (*Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum*) | *ó* + noun (*Trazei ao Senhor, ó filhos de Deus*) | open | Ps 28:1: the Latin tells the vocative from the accusative by case, and the two cola are built alike; *ó* supplies the case. DRB *O ye*, MS1932 *ó*. Distinct from the *Senhor* vocative (glossary: no *ó*). Passed the Latinist twice. |

| aríes | carneiro (*filhos de carneiros*) | open | Ps 28:1 *fílios aríetum* (υἱοὺς κριῶν — the Latin's line with the Greek; the Hebrew doubles 'sons of God'): *filhos* kept for the psalm's play fílii Dei / fílios aríetum / fílius unicórnium (28:6). 64:14, 65:15, 113:4, 113:6 (grep). MS1932 *tenros cordeiros* explains. |
| majéstas | majestade (*o Deus da majestade trovejou*) | working | Ps 28:3; 71:19 (grep: the only other place). Kept apart from magnificéntia → magnificência (28:4). |

| intercídere | dividir (*A voz do Senhor que divide a chama de fogo*) | open | Ps 28:7 only (grep); L&S 'cut asunder, divide' citing this verse; διακόπτοντος; DRB *divideth*. *cortar* may be heard as putting the flame out; *fender* literary; MS1932 *despede* is the Hebrew's sense. |

| Vox Dómini + genitive participle (*Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros*, 28:5, 7, 9) | *A voz do Senhor que quebra …* (relative clause; the acclamation stays a noun phrase) | open | Ps 28: the participles agree with *Dómini*; *que* can be heard with the voice or the Lord (the blind reader heard both). DRB and MS1932 make the voice the subject of a finite verb — the option. |

| diléctus (substantive) | o amado | open | Ps 28:6 only (grep); ὁ ἠγαπημένος; who is meant stays open (MS1932's note reads Israel). *o bem-amado* the option. Needs a copula when a verb precedes it (the blind reader's zeugma). |

| dilúvium; *inhabitáre facit* | dilúvio; *fazer habitar* (*O Senhor faz habitar o dilúvio*) | open | Ps 28:10 (31:6 *in dilúvio aquárum multárum*; 67:7a *qui inhabitáre facit* — grep). The Latin's causative left open (who dwells); the blind reader heard the doubt, as the Latin has it; MS1932 *faz do dilúvio a sua habitação* decides. |

| dícere glóriam | dizer glória (*todos dirão glória*) | open | Ps 28:9 *omnes dicent glóriam* (πᾶς τις λέγει δόξαν): open between the object spoken and the cry. *dirão: Glória!* (the Hebrew's reading) and DRB *his glory* are options. No reader remarked. |
formulas: | *Afférte Dómino … glóriam et honórem … afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus* (28:1–2; 95:7 *Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus*) | *Trazei ao Senhor … glória e honra … trazei ao Senhor glória ao seu nome* | open — Ps 28; **Ps 95:7 should copy it** |
| *adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus* (28:2 = 95:8, word for word, grep) | *adorai o Senhor no seu átrio santo* | open — Ps 28; **Ps 95:8 should copy it** |
